blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Capital allocation in emerging markets requires a different mental model from capital allocation in mature ones. Returns are higher, but so is the distribution of outcomes. A deal that looks attractive at the mean may hide a long left tail: a devaluation, a political change, a counterparty who cannot deliver what they promised, a regulatory shift that invalidates the structure you designed with such care.

The discipline that separates serious allocators from hopeful ones is scenario pricing. Every deal is priced not just in its central case but in a stressed case — and the allocation is sized so that even the stressed case is survivable. Were we to run only the central case, as most spreadsheets quietly do, we would be taking on risks we had not priced for.

Equally important is time horizon. Emerging markets punish short thinking. A business decided on the basis of one strong quarter, without regard to the cycle, will usually be regretted by the time the cycle turns. The patient allocator waits for cycles, respects them, and sizes positions so that even the worst year still leaves capital available for the best one.

items.q: According to the text, why does a deal that is attractive "at the mean" still deserve caution?
options: It cannot be priced in a spreadsheet
Its central case is impossible to model
It may hide a long left tail of severe outcomes
It usually offers lower returns than mature markets
items.why: "A deal that looks attractive at the mean may hide a long left tail" — a média esconde os cenários extremos ruins.

items.q: What is "scenario pricing" said to achieve?
options: It replaces the need for a time horizon
It removes all political risk from a deal
It prices the deal in both a central and a stressed case
It guarantees the highest possible return
items.why: "Every deal is priced not just in its central case but in a stressed case."

items.q: "Were we to run only the central case… we would be taking on risks we had not priced for." This suggests the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Allocations should survive the stressed case
Emerging markets have a wider distribution of outcomes
The central case alone is a sufficient basis for sizing a deal
Patience is rewarded across a full cycle
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto argumenta que confiar só no cenário central deixa riscos por precificar.

items.q: What does the phrase "as most spreadsheets quietly do" imply about common practice?
options: Spreadsheets are more reliable than judgement
Analysts deliberately overstate downside risk
Ignoring the stressed case is widespread but rarely admitted
Central-case modelling is a recent innovation
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" sugere uma prática comum e não reconhecida — rodar só o caso central.

items.q: How should the reader understand "size for the worst year, then the best one still arrives with capital available"?
options: Avoid emerging markets until the cycle turns
Treat every year as equally likely to be the best
Concentrate all capital in the single strongest quarter
Position so downside years never exhaust the capital needed for upside years
items.why: Inferência: dimensionar pela pior fase preserva capital para aproveitar a melhor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentando o novo investimento à banca de aprovação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. What I'm putting in front of you today is a proposed entry into an emerging-market trade operation, and I want to be candid about how we've sized it. I've run three scenarios, not one.

In the central case, the returns are genuinely attractive — comfortably ahead of anything we could earn in a mature market. But I'd ask you not to anchor on that number. In the stressed case, I've assumed a sharp devaluation of the local currency, a counterparty who delivers late, and a regulatory shift that reopens the contract. Under those assumptions the return falls hard, but — and this is the point — the position still survives. We do not lose capital we cannot afford to lose.

What we have deliberately avoided is deciding this on the strength of one quarter. If it were not for the cycle, I'd size this larger. But the cycle will turn, and a position that looks brilliant today can be the one you regret in eighteen months. So I've sized it to be patient — small enough that the worst year leaves us with capital intact, and ready for the year the cycle rewards us.

I'm asking for approval of the stressed-case size, not the central-case size. That distinction is the whole recommendation.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many scenarios has James run for the deal?
options: Three scenarios
As many as the spreadsheet allows
Two, both optimistic
One central case only
items.why: "I've run three scenarios, not one."

items.q: What does James assume in the stressed case?
options: A sharp devaluation, a late counterparty and a regulatory shift
A booming quarter and rising demand
A stable currency and a reliable counterparty
No change from the central case
items.why: "a sharp devaluation… a counterparty who delivers late… a regulatory shift that reopens the contract."

items.q: Why does James tell the board not to "anchor on" the central-case number?
options: Because it ignores the downside that the stressed case exposes
Because the cycle has already turned against it
Because it is the size he is actually asking them to approve
Because it understates the true return
items.why: Inferência: ele contrasta o caso central com o estressado justamente para não decidirem só pelo número bom.

items.q: What does James mean by "If it were not for the cycle, I'd size this larger"?
options: He has no view on the cycle at all
The cycle guarantees a large return
He wants to cancel the deal entirely
The cycle is the only reason he is keeping the position modest
items.why: Inferência: a estrutura hipotética diz que, sem o risco de ciclo, ele investiria mais — logo o ciclo é o freio.

items.q: What exactly is James asking the board to approve?
options: A delay until the cycle turns
The stressed-case size
The largest size the model permits
The central-case size
items.why: "I'm asking for approval of the stressed-case size, not the central-case size."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The committee reviewed our capital allocation across the region." Capital allocation is…
options: the office budget for the finance team
the deciding of where and how much capital to deploy
the currency held in local accounts
the total revenue booked in a quarter
items.why: Capital allocation = alocação de capital: decidir onde e quanto capital aplicar.

items.q: "A deal can look sound at the mean yet be dangerous in its left tail." The left tail refers to…
options: the earliest cash flows
the most likely, average outcome
the region of rare, severely negative outcomes
the upside scenario
items.why: Left tail = cauda esquerda: a faixa dos resultados raros e muito ruins.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A sudden ___ of the local currency wiped out the margin overnight."
options: allocation
horizon
devaluation
cycle
items.why: Devaluation = desvalorização da moeda, que corroeu a margem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We priced the trade across every ___, not just the case we hoped for."
options: scenario
quarter
spreadsheet
counterparty
items.why: Scenario pricing = precificar em cada cenário, e não só no esperado.

items.q: "A serious allocator respects the cycle instead of chasing one strong quarter." An allocator is someone who…
options: markets the fund to new investors
decides how capital is deployed and sized
negotiates the legal contract
audits the accounts after the fact
items.why: Allocator = alocador: quem decide como e quanto capital investir.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em comitês de investimento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The investment committee still has to sign off on the stressed-case size." To sign off on means to…
options: leak to the market
raise informal doubts
postpone indefinitely
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two members pushed back on the central-case assumptions." They…
options: rewrote the whole model
resisted or challenged them
ignored them completely
approved them at once
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to hold off on the second tranche until the cycle turns." To hold off on means to…
options: delegate it to the desk
delay it deliberately
cancel it permanently
double it immediately
items.why: Hold off on = adiar de propósito, esperar o momento certo.

items.q: "None of these tweaks will move the needle on the downside." This means they will…
options: breach the mandate
take years to measure
not make a noticeable difference
trigger a devaluation
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "If the cycle turns hard, the counterparty may not follow through on delivery." To follow through means to…
options: hedge the currency exposure
renegotiate the price
carry the commitment to completion
report the breach to the regulator
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado, cumprir o compromisso.
